correctness.rationale: For every a,b>=2 and u,w,v>0 with u,w<=2v, the exact Hilbert variance identity yields D²v²>=((a-1)u²/(2a)+(b-1)w²/(2b)). An explicit pair of centered orthogonal regular simplices with adjustable orthogonal centroid translation realizes max(v²,Σ) on every cross pair. At equality the nonnegative slack terms in the variance identity vanish individually, proving intra-orbit tightness, centroid equality and uniform cross distances; double-centering determines orthogonality, uniqueness up to isometry, and exact affine ranks a+b-2 or a+b-1 at the correct boundary. The split graph has u=1,w=2,v=1 and Σ>=5/4>1. The actual packaged checker.py independently replayed 2448 rational Gram examples, 448 centroid-identity instances, and 244464 exact tests. Finite tests supplement the all-real-parameter argument.

value.rationale: The exact threshold and full optimizer/dimension classification solve a naturally motivated family of independently weighted two-equilateral-cluster metric spaces, including complete split graph shortest-path metrics, rather than an arbitrary slice. The strict-distortion regime forces shared centroids and exact dimension a+b-2; the isometric regime has an exact dimension jump a+b-2 versus a+b-1. This equality rigidity is additional structural content beyond a basic scalar substitution into Robertson’s equal-block formula, and explicitly identifies nonregular graph invariants. The scope is finite and two-block only; no broad downstream theorem is asserted.
